mechanism_narrative: A lower federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) indicates accommodative monetary policy, reducing discount rates applied to equity cash flows and generating positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The Rank IC between FEDFUNDS and 20-day S&P 500 returns is negative or below 0.03 in any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A rising unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 6.5% signals economic weakness and declining corporate earnings prospects, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When UNRATE exceeds 6.5%, the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: The joint decline in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and rise in unemployment (UNRATE) signals a recessionary environment, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When FEDFUNDS declines and UNRATE rises, the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle expansions, high consumer spending (RSAFS) and strong housing starts (HOUST) indicate economic overheating, increasing the likelihood of Fed rate hikes and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In the late-cycle expansion regime, the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A rising labor force (PAYEMS) indicates economic strength and higher corporate profits, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The Rank IC between PAYEMS and 5-day S&P 500 returns is negative or below 0.03 in any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 100 signals a contraction in the real economy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: When INDPRO falls below 100, the 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: High consumer spending (RSAFS) combined with stable or rising monetary policy (FEDFUNDS) signals an overheating economy, increasing the probability of Fed tightening and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When RSAFS exceeds 550,000 and FEDFUNDS is not declining, the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: During monetary tightening cycles, when the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) exceeds 0.5%, the S&P 500 tends to underperform due to higher discount rates and reduced equity valuations, leading to negative forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When FEDFUNDS exceeds 0.5%, the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of cases.
